definitions._authored: The league does not publish its rules for these measures. Every definition below is authored here, and each is also computed under a second defensible rule so the disagreement can be read beside the number. These figures are NOT the league's.
definitions.closest_defender: nearest opposing player to the SHOOTER, in 2D, at the frame the ball leaves the hand. THE SUBJECT IS THE GEOMETRIC SHOOTER, not the player the record filed the shot under: the body nearest the ball at the release frame is bound there and then followed backwards through the gather and the whole approach, so both instants and every frame between them describe one person. Where that body has no row in a frame the frame is empty rather than filled with somebody else. The two attributions are independent and their agreement rate ships as recovery.attribution_agreement; the defender is deliberately NOT bound, because a switch is a real event in a closing distance, and each track frame carries an anonymous defender slot so a change of body is visible instead of drawn through. Also taken at the gather 10 frames (0.4 s) earlier, on that same bound body
definitions.buckets: the league's own four published categories: 0-2, 2-4, 4-6, 6+ ft
definitions.sentinel_corroboration: the one measurement in this file whose subject is the SHOT RECORD rather than the tracking feed. seasons.json says the record files a whole category of shot on a single coordinate; that rested on one read of one database, and every other source available today - including a live stats.nba.com query - is another read of the SAME database. This asks a DIFFERENT INSTRUMENT. The join between the two constrains the BALL (reconciles tests the ball at release against the filed coordinate within 6 ft); the evidence here is a different variable, the SHOOTER'S FEET, which the join never reads. That BOUNDS the dispersion from above rather than leaving it free - the ball is above the shooter - so it cannot PRODUCE the dispersion, and the argument rests on the control instead: if the coordinate were a real location the pile would be TIGHTER than shots the record placed one by one, because those have genuinely different true positions and the pile would share one. It is not. The control is like-for-like because it has to be - the pile is almost entirely dunks and the dunk family is where this project's own release detector is weakest (see disagreement.by_action) - so it is restricted-area dunks the record placed individually: same instrument, same season, same games, same action family, same detector. `dispersed` reads `cells_per_shot` against 0.5, which separates readings four orders of magnitude apart. `at_the_rim` asks the other half of the question - if the feed put these shots somewhere else entirely the record would be placing them WRONGLY rather than declining to place them - and asks it like-for-like, against the control's own spread rather than an absolute radius. SCOPE, stated rather than buried: the public tracking release covers ONE of the six seasons that file a displaced pile, and `sentinel.filed` against `filed_season` is how much of that season the corpus reaches
definitions.hero: one of the four shots the opening beat draws, one per published category, chosen by the tightest corroboration with the record. A hero must BE one confrontation: a complete track, no frame gap, and no step over 3.0 ft between consecutive frames - for the bound shooter or within any one defender slot - because 40 ms of feed cannot carry a body further than that and a track that says otherwise is two bodies spliced. The same limit governs `distance_run`; it is stated here as well so the figure the continuity of a drawn track rests on is disclosed where the track is defined
definitions.touch: ball within 3.5 ft of its nearest player for at least 10 frames (0.4 s) and at most 12.0 s, across UNBROKEN FEED: the chain is cut at every period change and at every gap wider than 2x the feed's own modal frame spacing, so no touch spans a quarter break or a dropout; also computed at 3.0 ft
definitions.drive: one touch in which the ball is sampled at or beyond 20.0 ft from a hoop and then, LATER IN THE SAME TOUCH, at or within 10.0 ft. Order is part of the definition: taking a maximum and a minimum over the touch, as this did, counts a player carrying the ball away from the rim as driving to it. `inventory.drives_unordered` is that undirected reading, kept so the difference can be read
definitions.pass: two consecutive touches by different players of the same team, in the same period, no more than 1200 ms apart. The gap is authored and the distribution it was drawn from ships as `pass_gap_ms`: it is single-peaked with a long flat dead-ball tail, and this is that distribution's p90. `inventory.passes_alt_gap` counts the same events at 2000 ms, where the density falls to within an order of magnitude of the tail
definitions.distance_run: summed per-player displacement between two frames in which that player was actually recorded, back to back, within one unbroken stretch of feed. Steps over 3.0 ft are dropped as gaps or identity swaps, and every player's last position is forgotten at a period change or a dropout - without that, a player standing near where they stood one period earlier has the difference counted as running
definitions.occupancy: where the BALL is, per frame, in the same distance bands the shot record's own attempts are read in - available only here, because this is the only period with a ball to follow
definitions.recovery: a shot is measured only if a release found from physics lands within 6.0 ft of where the record independently filed it; the join is checked by geometry, never asserted
definitions.recovery.failures.no tracking event: the record filed a shot for which no release could be recovered from the feed at this game's calibrated event offset - either the feed carries no event for it, or it carries one in which no ball reached the rim
definitions.recovery.failures.anchor residual too la: a release was found but landed more than 6.0 ft from the filed coordinate; see `disagreement`, which counts these rather than discarding them - most are the two records genuinely differing, not a detection failure
definitions.event_offset: tracking eventId == shotdetail GAME_EVENT_ID holds for most games and fails silently for a minority, where the two numberings differ by a small constant. Calibrated once per game by letting that game's detected releases vote; one integer per game from ~150 shots, never a per-shot fit. Searched over +/-12, and a winner ON that boundary is REJECTED rather than shipped, because an argmax at the edge is the signature of a peak outside the search. A non-zero winner must also be carried by at least 25 reconciled shots, clear the straight join by 1.5x, and beat its own runner-up by 0.15; zero faces the same comparison and is never accepted without one. The comparison is made over EVERY release the game gives up, never over the releases sitting at anchor event ids - on that set offset zero has a candidate anchor for every member by construction and its rivals do not, so it cannot lose. Then it is validated: even-numbered tracking events calibrate, odd ones check, and `held_out_agreement` is how often the two halves named the same integer. A half whose argmax was refused NAMED NOTHING and is not counted as an answer
definitions.coverage: 632 of the 2015-16 season's 1,230 games - the first half only, and schedule-biased

votes.population: games whose argmax is non-zero, i.e. where the floor is reached

recovery.held_out_note: half a game's releases calibrate and half validate, split on the parity of the tracking event id, over EVERY release in the game. The aggregate rate is dominated by games needing no offset; read held_out_by_outcome instead. A half whose argmax was refused named nothing and is counted under held_out_refused_halves rather than as an answer

bias.why: a release is recovered by following the ball back from the rim, so shots that reach the rim are over-represented and made shots all reach it; the recovered set shoots better than the league did and every figure taken from it inherits that
disclosure: FOUND FROM THE RIM · THEY GO IN 50.9% AGAINST THE SEASON'S 45.2%

frame_gap_ms.note: consecutive same-period frame spacings across the corpus, in ms; the last key is everything over 200 ms. The threshold a touch, a pass or a stride may not cross is 2x each game's own modal spacing

pass_gap_ms.note: gaps between consecutive same-team, same-period touches, binned to 40 ms; key k counts gaps in [40k, 40k+40), and the last key is everything above

measures_bin.fields: x, y, dx, dy (int16 tenths, hoop at origin); dist (uint16 tenths ft, never clipped); bucket; made; day

sentinel_corroboration.evidence: the shooter's feet at release. The join BOUNDS this dispersion and cannot PRODUCE it - it holds the ball within 6 ft of the filed coordinate, and the ball sits above the shooter - so the bound runs AGAINST the finding rather than for it. The work is done by the like-for-like control: if the coordinate were a real location the pile would be TIGHTER than shots the record placed one by one, because those have genuinely different true positions and the pile would share one. It is not tighter. Size-matched, it is indistinguishable

control.label: restricted-area dunks the record placed individually
